request.content:
You help a human prepare a quote request. Read the entire request
and clarification conversation. Decide whether its meaning is clear enough to
prepare an accurate request. Notice conflicting requirements, implausible scope,
ambiguous units, and assumptions that would materially change the quote. Ask the
human a focused question in your own words when their judgment or information is
needed. Check for multiple independent issues across the whole request, not just
the first inconsistency. Keep all unresolved issues in view after every answer.
You may group closely related questions; do not complete while a material issue
remains unresolved. Explain the concrete uncertainty. This is a conversation, not a required
field checklist. Do not silently repair contradictions or invent requirements,
prices, feasibility guarantees, or human answers. Reconsider the request after
every answer; an unclear answer may need another question. Complete without a
question when the request is already coherent. Completion summarizes the agreed
scope and any explicitly accepted uncertainty; it does not send a quote or
promise supplier acceptance. Return exactly one QuoteDecision tool call.

{"initial_request": {"name": "Alex", "email": "alex@example.com", "service": "Print 500 individually addressed invitations. Use the exact same text on every copy; no variable printing.", "quantity": 500, "recipients": "650 guests, each must receive their own invitation.", "delivery": "One batch to our office; we will mail them ourselves."}, "conversation": []}

content.name: QuoteDecision
content.arguments: {"action":"ask","reason":"Two material requirements conflict: the request specifies 500 invitations, but says all 650 guests must receive one, and it also requests individual addressing while requiring identical text with no variable printing. The quantity and addressing method need to be confirmed before an accurate quote request can be prepared.","text":"Should the quoted quantity be 650 invitations (one per guest) or 500? Also, do you want guest names/addresses printed on each invitation or envelope, or should all pieces remain completely identical and be supplied unaddressed for you to mail?"}

args.reason: Two material requirements conflict: the request specifies 500 invitations, but says all 650 guests must receive one, and it also requests individual addressing while requiring identical text with no variable printing. The quantity and addressing method need to be confirmed before an accurate quote request can be prepared.
args.text: Should the quoted quantity be 650 invitations (one per guest) or 500? Also, do you want guest names/addresses printed on each invitation or envelope, or should all pieces remain completely identical and be supplied unaddressed for you to mail?

{"initial_request": {"name": "Alex", "email": "alex@example.com", "service": "Print 500 individually addressed invitations. Use the exact same text on every copy; no variable printing.", "quantity": 500, "recipients": "650 guests, each must receive their own invitation.", "delivery": "One batch to our office; we will mail them ourselves."}, "conversation": [{"question": "Should the quoted quantity be 650 invitations (one per guest) or 500? Also, do you want guest names/addresses printed on each invitation or envelope, or should all pieces remain completely identical and be supplied unaddressed for you to mail?", "answer": "There are 500 households among the 650 guests. Include 500 printed envelopes; we will supply a spreadsheet of names and addresses. Deliver one batch to our office, and we will mail them ourselves."}]}

content.name: QuoteDecision
content.arguments: {"action":"complete","reason":"The quantity and mailing-unit discrepancy is resolved: there are 500 households, so the order is for 500 identical invitations. Variable information is limited to each household's name and address printed on its envelope, with 500 envelopes supplied and the address spreadsheet provided by the customer. Delivery is one batch to the office for customer mailing.","text":"Please quote 500 invitations, all with identical text, plus 500 printed envelopes addressed with the supplied household names and addresses. The 650 guests are grouped into 500 households, with one invitation per household. Deliver the complete batch to our office; we will mail it ourselves."}

args.reason: The quantity and mailing-unit discrepancy is resolved: there are 500 households, so the order is for 500 identical invitations. Variable information is limited to each household's name and address printed on its envelope, with 500 envelopes supplied and the address spreadsheet provided by the customer. Delivery is one batch to the office for customer mailing.
args.text: Please quote 500 invitations, all with identical text, plus 500 printed envelopes addressed with the supplied household names and addresses. The 650 guests are grouped into 500 households, with one invitation per household. Deliver the complete batch to our office; we will mail it ourselves.
